title: Malware Evasion Susceptibility detected in GPT-4o during LLM Benchmark (malwaregen.Evasion)
description: LLM benchmarking results for model gpt-4o show a high-risk exposure to malware-generation evasion probes. The malwaregen.Evasion probe was used, with 11 hits out of 48 tests (22.92% hit rate). The probe detected evasion behavior despite the detector being malwaregen.AnyCode. This indicates potential for adversaries to prompt the model to bypass content safeguards or assist in malware-related activities.
suggested_fix: 1) Strengthen input and prompt filtering to block malware-related prompts and evasion attempts. 2) Enforce strict output sanitization and disallow generation of executable or malware payloads (code, scripts, payloads). 3) Integrate an adversarial/bypass testing suite into development and CI to routinely test for malware-evasion prompts; patch gaps promptly. 4) Apply policy-driven guardrails that prevent instruction-following for harmful activities, including malware creation or distribution. 5) Implement runtime monitoring and anomaly detection for evasion patterns; alert and throttle when suspicious prompts are detected. 6) Restrict printing or exporting of certain sensitive content; consider a safe-mode mode for high-risk scenarios.
